title: Release-train bump alignment canvas and OKR-mapped cutover plan for runtime/console/API
creator: Aisha Kumar
acceptance_criteria: A single cross-team calendar (canonical source) is published and linked in the Launch Confluence page
Per-surface runbook (runtime, console, API) with cutover owner, rollback criteria, and SLA gates is created and reviewed
OKR mapping demonstrates how the release bump contributes to Q2 reliability and cost-efficiency targets
Automated alerts and dashboards for ticketed rollout gates are wired to the Launch Ops Slack channel
All listed dependencies have owners and signed-off contingency plans (capacity and fallback models)
description:
Objective: Create an "alignment canvas" that maps a targeted release-train bump across runtime / console / API surfaces to the company OKRs, and produce a pragmatic cutover plan that reduces cross-team ambiguity during the week-of-launch.

Scope:
- Produce a visual alignment canvas (one-page) that shows: feature bundles, owners, OKR contribution, capacity reservations, and critical rollback gates.
- Draft per-surface cutover runbooks (concise checklists) oriented around SLO gates, model fallbacks, and communication protocols.
- Coordinate a single canonical launch calendar and embed it in the Launch Orchestration Confluence with links to PRs, test dashboards, and on-call rosters.

Why this ticket: Recent rollouts showed repeated friction between runtime autoscaling decisions and console feature toggles, causing slack time during cutover and avoidable rollbacks. This work ties the technical bumps to the business OKRs so stakeholders can prioritize risk mitigations.

Deliverables:
- Alignment canvas (PNG + editable Google Slide)
- 3 runbook checklists (runtime, console, API) and a consolidated one-page extraction for the launch conductor
- Calendar artifact (Google Calendar + ICS export) with ownership metadata and blackout windows
- Linked checklist in the Release Confluence page and the Launch Ops Slack channel

Links to artifacts and references:
- Confluence draft: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/LO/pages/LaunchAlignmentCanvas
- Draft runbooks (Drive): https://drive.redwood.com/drive/folders/launch-runbooks-2026
- Canary stress-test dashboard: https://console.redwood.com/dashboards/canary-stress-2026
- Recent postmortem that motivated this: https://redwood.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/IR/pages/PR-2025-12-runtime-cutover-postmortem

Stakeholders: PM (Aisha Kumar), Runtime ENG (Marcus Lee), Console PM (Lena Park), Platform SRE (Diego Martinez), Product Design reviewer (Sofia Nguyen).
rollout_strategy: Staged release-train bump: week -3 shadow traffic and metric baselines; week -1 canary cohorts in us-east-1 and eu-west-1; week-of progressive lane openings keyed to SLO thresholds (latency P50/P95, error rate, cost-per-token). If any gate trips, automatic fallback to prior model variant + page incident channel and hold further cohort expansion.
comments: 2026-01-12 | Marcus Lee: Kickoff complete. Runtime team will validate capacity hedges for the 20% bump by 2026-02-10. Action: ENG to produce capacity runbook and worst-case pricing delta.

2026-01-15 | Lena Park: Console team agrees to freeze non-critical UI changes during week-of; will maintain feature flag matrix. Requesting a clear list of API migrations that could affect front-end integrations.

2026-01-22 | Diego Martinez: Noted two operational gaps from postmortem: (1) missing automated rollback on KV-cache corruption, (2) insufficient cross-region traffic shadowing. SRE will schedule a remediation spike (ENG-51720).

2026-01-27 | Aisha Kumar: Draft alignment canvas pasted to Confluence (link above). Seeking review from security/compliance for any export controls or audit log requirements. Please leave inline comments by 2026-01-30.
2026-01-30 | Sofia Nguyen: Design reviewed the canvas; suggested clarifying the 'owner' field to separate technical owner vs business stakeholder. Updated slide deck and reuploaded to Drive.

2026-02-02 | Marcus Lee: Capacity tests completed at 85% of expected traffic bump. Identified a kernel scheduling hotspot at seq_len > 2k in eu-west-1 — ENG-61902 created. Recommend gating the eu-west-1 cohort until mitigation is merged.

2026-02-03 | Aisha Kumar: Consolidated sign-offs: PMs and SRE have signed the runbook. Next steps: finalize calendar ICS and announce the launch conductor rota by 2026-02-05. Assigned follow-up action to Marcus (ENG-61902) and Diego (ENG-51720).
notes_for_ops: Use the Launch Ops Slack channel (#launch-ops) for real-time cutover comms
Primary rollback trigger: sustained >3% increase in token error rate or >30% degradation in P95 latency for 10m window
Backup model variants and routing policies are listed in the runtime catalog (see Confluence)
